comparisons.title: Moonstack
comparisons.review: A midnight block club in mint and navy. On a 390 × 844 phone, the board and touch controls fit on screen. Its checks exercise line scores, hold, pause, touch input, restart confirmation and storage failures.

comparisons.label: Astra · Codex CLI
comparisons.title: Afterglow
comparisons.review: Cream, teal and lime with a distinctive editorial layout. Sound, personal bests and a three-piece queue add character. Its checks exercise movement, hold, line clearing, level changes and game over. Touch controls sit further down the page.

comparisonNote: One shared brief. Identical starting files. Astra at medium effort in both harnesses. These are the files each delivered.
sharedBrief:
Make me a beautiful, complete falling-block puzzle game in one self-contained HTML file called arcade.html.

Make it feel like a little arcade game someone would actually want to keep. Choose a memorable name and visual style. Be creative: add thoughtful touches and delightful extras where they improve the experience.

It needs a real playable board, falling pieces that move and rotate, line clearing, scoring, a next-piece preview, hold, pause/resume, restart, and a game-over state. Include clear keyboard controls and touch controls that work on a phone. Make the interface comfortable on a small screen and attractive on a desktop. Sound is optional; if you add it, include a mute control.

Everything must work offline from this single file: no downloads, build step, external assets, or third-party dependencies. Use inline CSS and classic inline JavaScript. Keep the supplied package.json and test/delivery.test.js unchanged. Those starter tests check delivery packaging only. Add your own meaningful checks, inspect your work, and fix what you find before you finish.
conditions: Each fresh build received ten minutes. Two supplied checks cover packaging; the agents wrote their own additional tests. We played the unedited files in Chromium at desktop, 390 px and 320 px widths. The Codex build took 404.9 s; the completed factory build took 420.2 s. The factory attempt follows fixes to preview guidance and mobile viewport handling; an earlier attempt reached the time limit. All attempts are retained in the experiment record. Native Codex overlapped other local work; the completed factory run was serialized.
usageNote: Tokens come from saved usage receipts. Fresh input excludes cached input; output includes reported reasoning tokens. These runs used a Codex account. Token counts are measured; no per-run dollar charge was supplied. The estimate range treats fresh input as ordinary input through all cache writes; cache-write usage was not reported separately. Preview tools can also use local vision, which was not separately metered in the Astra-only attempts.
